spec: E1 — the shared-dependency layer. First-class common-cause nodes whose degradation or loss fires MANY risk patterns in the same trial-year. This is the axis pattern-to-pattern cascade edges cannot express: an AWS regional failure, a customer-auth-plane outage, an etcd quorum loss are not contagion BETWEEN risks — they are one structural event underneath several risks at once.
provenance_note: Annual event frequencies are OPERATOR JUDGMENT anchored to named public incidents — a synthetic demonstrator has no internal dependency-failure history to fit. Fan-out maps (which patterns fire, how hard) encode platform-archetype topology: multi-region, ~500 K8s apps, first-party customer identity, external payment rails. Production replaces frequencies with fitted internal/industry data and fan-outs with the real service-dependency graph. r29 RECALIBRATION: fan-out severity multipliers capped at 2.0 (were up to 3.0) — pattern severity distributions are already material-incident calibrated with their own lognormal tails; multipliers beyond 2 double-count tail mass the distribution carries. Dependency-injected draws are ALSO excluded from the E5 co-movement multiplier for the same double-counting reason. r29: induced_incidents capped at 1 — one structural event yields ONE material incident per affected pattern (the multi-PATTERN spread in the same trial-year is the common-cause mechanism; multi-count per pattern double-counted the event against pattern distributions that already price severity).

nodes.name: Primary cloud region
nodes.mitigation_note: Multi-region HA absorbs part of a loss event (the recover-function control row already carries the 'Regional-failure tabletop' gap); the loss frequency below is the RESIDUAL broad-impact rate after that architecture, not the raw provider rate.

anchors.name: AWS us-east-1 outage
anchors.summary: Internal-network device congestion took down a broad slice of us-east-1 for ~7 hours; control-plane APIs unavailable, downstream SaaS worldwide degraded.

anchors.name: AWS us-east-1 Lambda/STS event
anchors.summary: Multi-hour us-east-1 degradation of Lambda, STS and console — auth-adjacent blast radius beyond one service.

anchors.name: AWS S3 us-east-1 outage
anchors.summary: S3 disruption cascaded into thousands of dependent services — the canonical shared-region common cause.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.08/yr ≈ 1-in-12yr RESIDUAL broad-impact rate after multi-region HA — major-provider regional events run near-annual industry-wide (us-east-1 2021/2023, S3 2017); the judgment is the HA haircut, not the provider rate. degraded 0.8/yr ≈ the near-annual class, embedded in base pattern rates per dep_attribution. OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.
nodes.failover_basis: E5 — the multi-region term: when the region loss fires, with p=0.25 the FAILOVER ITSELF fails (partial DNS cutover, warm-standby capacity shortfall, split-brain on promotion) and the event ESCALATES ×1.5 across its fan-out. Basis: the recover-function's own DR-exercise rows credit failover well below 100%; GitHub 2018-10-21 (failover produced divergent writes), TSB 2018 (migration cutover failure class). OPERATOR_CALIBRATED; production fits from live failover exercise pass rates.

nodes.name: Customer identity & session plane (first-party)
nodes.mitigation_note: First-party authN/session/token issuance for the platform's OWN customers — not workforce SSO. Loss locks customers out of accounts and funds in real time; degraded verification opens the account-takeover / recovery-abuse surface while support channels saturate. E2 adds the BLINDNESS mode — the plane is UP but verification is degraded (weakened fallback auth, degraded risk-scoring, session-validation failures): an account-takeover / recovery-abuse wave, not an outage. Distinct from routine degradation (which stays embedded in base rates per dep_attribution): blindness is a structural common-cause state across every login at once.

anchors.name: Auth0 global outage
anchors.summary: Customer-identity-as-a-service outage — every relying application's login broke simultaneously; the pure form of this node's loss mode.

anchors.name: Retail-brokerage login failures under volume
anchors.summary: Multiple major retail brokerages' customer login/session planes degraded or failed during meme-stock volume spikes — customers locked out of positions at the worst possible moment; regulatory and trust consequences followed.

anchors.name: Coinbase outage during volatility
anchors.summary: Customer access failures during a market-wide crypto drawdown — the correlation between load, volatility, and identity-plane failure is the point.

anchors.name: 0ktapus / Twilio smishing wave
anchors.summary: One phishing kit against SMS-OTP verification rolled through 130+ companies — degraded verification exploited industrially, platform-wide, at once.

anchors.name: Okta support-system session-token replay
anchors.summary: Stolen session tokens bypassed authentication entirely — the plane was up; the verification was blind.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.15/yr ≈ 1-in-7yr full customer-auth outage for a first-party plane under volatility load (Auth0 2021 for the vendor class; 2021-01 brokerage login failures for the first-party-under-load class). blindness 0.2/yr ≈ 1-in-5yr platform-wide degraded-verification state (0ktapus 2022 rolled 130+ firms in one campaign). OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.

nodes.name: API registry / gateway & service discovery
nodes.mitigation_note: The service-to-service spine: gateway config, discovery, routing, internal authZ between services. A bad push here is a single event that makes MANY healthy services unreachable or mis-routed at once; deploys and rollbacks stall because the control path itself is degraded.

anchors.name: Fastly global outage
anchors.summary: One customer config push triggered a latent bug — most of the global edge went down in minutes; gateway-plane loss in its purest public form.

anchors.name: Cloudflare WAF regex incident
anchors.summary: A single rule deployment consumed global CPU at the gateway layer — worldwide 502s; the control path took down the data path.

anchors.name: Cloudflare API/dashboard outage
anchors.summary: Control-plane datacenter failure degraded the API/config plane for ~2 days — services ran, but nothing could be changed, scaled, or fixed.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.1/yr ≈ 1-in-10yr bad-push/config event at the gateway plane (Fastly 2021 and Cloudflare 2019 were single-push global events; per-firm rate is the judgment). OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.

nodes.name: Kubernetes control plane / etcd
nodes.mitigation_note: etcd quorum or apiserver loss: running pods keep serving (data plane persists) but scheduling, scaling, self-healing, admission and deploys stop — degradation compounds with every node failure the platform can no longer route around. Cell/multi-cluster architecture bounds one cluster's blast radius; the frequency below is per-platform (any Tier-1-carrying cluster).

anchors.name: Reddit Pi-Day outage
anchors.summary: K8s upgrade broke a legacy node-route dependency — control-plane confusion took the site down for hours; the public postmortem is a canonical control-plane failure study.

anchors.name: Datadog multi-region outage
anchors.summary: An OS auto-update rebooted nodes fleet-wide across regions and clouds — the orchestration layer itself became the common cause across supposedly independent regions.

anchors.name: GitHub metadata-store partition
anchors.summary: 43 seconds of network partition in the coordination layer → ~24 hours of degraded service — coordination-plane loss outlasts the trigger by orders of magnitude.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.07/yr ≈ 1-in-14yr quorum/apiserver loss on a Tier-1-carrying cluster, per platform across the cell fleet (Reddit 2023 and Datadog 2023 are the observed class; multi-cluster isolation is why loss is rarer than degraded 0.7/yr). OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.

nodes.name: Workforce identity provider (SSO)
nodes.mitigation_note: Engineer/operator SSO. Distinct failure content from the customer plane: blast radius is internal tooling AND the response function itself — responders locked out of the consoles they need to fix the outage. E2 models the recursion as a mechanism: an active loss multiplies EVERY severity that trial-year ×1.25 (see response_recursion), on top of the RP-12 injection.

anchors.name: Okta support-system breach
anchors.summary: Compromise at the workforce-identity vendor propagated to downstream customers — the IdP as shared attack surface, not just shared availability.

anchors.name: Azure AD global outage
anchors.summary: Authentication outage locked users out of M365 and dependent apps for hours — workforce identity as a single global choke point.

anchors.name: Okta/Lapsus$ incident
anchors.summary: Third-party support-engineer compromise at the IdP — weeks of downstream customer investigation for one vendor event.

anchors.name: Meta global outage (BGP + internal lockout)
anchors.summary: The outage locked engineers out of the very tools and buildings needed to fix it — the definitive response-recursion event: the fix path shared the failed dependency.

response_recursion.note: E2 — the recursion, as a mechanism: a trial-year containing a workforce-IdP LOSS multiplies the severity of EVERY incident that year ×1.25 — responders are locked out of the consoles they need to respond with, so everything that goes wrong that year goes wrong for longer. Operator judgment, anchored, bounded by the recursion_off lever.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.05/yr ≈ 1-in-20yr full workforce-SSO outage (Azure AD 2021 class); the compromise anchors (Okta 2022/2023) inform severity and the recursion, not this availability rate. OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.

nodes.name: Primary transactional datastore cluster
nodes.mitigation_note: The ledger/order/account store of record. Loss is availability plus INTEGRITY exposure — split-brain and mid-failover writes are how an availability event becomes a data event; reconciliation cost persists long after service restores.

anchors.name: GitHub MySQL failover split
anchors.summary: Cross-region failover produced divergent writes — restoring consistency, not connectivity, drove the ~24h impact.

anchors.name: AWS DynamoDB metadata outage
anchors.summary: Storage-layer metadata service degradation cascaded into dependent AWS services region-wide.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.06/yr ≈ 1-in-16yr store-of-record failover failure (GitHub 2018 split-brain, DynamoDB 2015) — rarer than region loss because the store rides ON the region node. OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.
nodes.failover_basis: E5: store-of-record promotion is the hardest failover in the platform — with p=0.3 a loss event escalates ×1.5 (split-brain, divergent writes, reconciliation tail: GitHub 2018-10-21 is the canonical case — 43s of partition, ~24h of impact BECAUSE the failover path itself misbehaved). OPERATOR_CALIBRATED.

nodes.name: External payments processor / card rails
nodes.mitigation_note: The money movement path the platform does not own. Loss means customer-visible payment failure with zero internal remediation lever — pure third-party concentration; the org_context already records that funding a second provider is a board-appetite question, not a TRC ticket.

anchors.name: Visa Europe outage
anchors.summary: A hardware failure at the card network declined a large share of European transactions for hours — merchants and issuers had no lever at all.

anchors.name: UK Faster Payments/bank rail incidents
anchors.summary: TSB migration failure class — payment-rail unavailability with days-long tail and regulatory aftermath.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.1/yr ≈ 1-in-10yr full rail outage from the firm's seat (Visa Europe 2018, TSB 2018 class) — external, so no architecture haircut applies; degraded 0.8/yr brownouts are embedded in base RP-07 rates. OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.

nodes.name: Security agent / endpoint vendor channel
nodes.mitigation_note: The trusted agent with fleet-wide reach and auto-update rights — a vendor content push is functionally an unreviewed global deploy. Rare, but the severity profile is the worst in the catalog because trust plus reach equals blast radius.

anchors.name: CrowdStrike Falcon content update
anchors.summary: One trusted security-vendor content push blue-screened ~8.5M Windows hosts globally — airlines, hospitals, banks; the definitive security-vendor-as-SPOF event.

anchors.name: SolarWinds Orion compromise
anchors.summary: The same trusted-channel reach exploited deliberately — the update path as supply-chain attack surface.

nodes.freq_basis: loss 0.04/yr ≈ 1-in-25yr catastrophic trusted-channel push (CrowdStrike 2024 is the single observed instance at full severity; SolarWinds 2020 for the deliberate form) — rarest in the catalog, worst severity profile. OPERATOR_CALIBRATED: rates are judgment anchored to the named public incidents; production fits from internal/industry dependency-failure history.

deferred_nodes.note: DECLARED DEFERRALS (external finding, Claude round-27: 'a catalog whose flagship mechanism cites a DNS incident while lacking a DNS node is a coherence seam'): the 8 shipped nodes are the starter set. Deferred node classes, named so their absence is a decision, not a blind spot: dns_resolution (the Meta 2021-10-04 anchor was a BGP/DNS event — its LOCKOUT mechanics are what workforce_idp carries; the routing-plane loss mode itself is deferred and partially folded into cloud_region/api_registry fan-outs), cert_pki_expiry (a top real-world cause class), observability_stack (the reflexive blindness dependency — when monitoring dies every level-KRI goes dark, RP-14's own thesis pointed at the model's instrumentation), kms_secrets, cdn_edge, service_mesh, message_bus, network_fabric. E5 adds tenant_isolation to the deferrals: account/tenant blast-radius topology (one tenant's failure crossing an isolation boundary) is a distinct axis from the shared planes priced here; the containment_boundary fields on nodes and edges carry the coarse version.
